title: KPerfIR: Towards a Open and Compiler-centric Ecosystem for GPU Kernel Performance Tooling on Modern AI Workloads
problem: GPU kernel profiling introduces significant overhead and measurement error, hindering performance analysis and optimization feedback during compiler-driven code generation
motivation: Accurate profiling with minimal overhead is critical for AI hardware because compiler passes need reliable performance data to make optimization decisions. High overhead profiling can skew measurements and delay iterative development cycles
method: Integrated profiling infrastructure built directly into the Triton compiler, providing fine-grained kernel performance measurements with instrumentation at compile-time to minimize runtime overhead
key_novelty: First profiling system to integrate directly into Triton compiler pipeline with only 8.2% measurement overhead and 2% error tolerance, enabling closed-loop compiler optimization
contributions: Integrated profiling infrastructure in Triton compiler reducing measurement overhead to 8.2%
Measurement error reduced to 2% of true performance metrics
Enables compiler passes to directly use profiling data for performance-driven optimization decisions
Eliminates separate profiling passes, improving developer iteration time
hardware_target: Any GPU supported by Triton compiler
limitations: Limited to Triton compiler ecosystem; measurement overhead still non-zero; applicability to other compiler frameworks unclear
